title: Balloons and Static Electricity
desc: The child rubs a balloon on a sweater and watches the tiny charges move, then sees the balloon stick to the sweater or wall and two charged balloons push apart.
how: Try it after rubbing a real balloon on hair, so the child can see what was happening that they could not see.

title: John Travoltage
desc: The child moves John's foot across a carpet so he collects charge, then moves his hand towards a door knob to make a spark jump and see when he gets a shock.
how: A quick, funny opener for static electricity and why we sometimes get small shocks.

title: Circuit Construction Kit: DC
desc: The child drags wires, batteries, bulbs and switches onto a workspace to build circuits, sees bulbs light up, and tests whether everyday objects conduct electricity.
how: Use alongside a real battery-and-bulb kit; the sim lets the child try circuits safely that would be hard to build at home.

title: States of Matter: Basics
desc: The child heats, cools and squeezes a container of atoms and molecules and watches them change between solid, liquid and gas.
how: Good right after melting ice or boiling water in the kitchen, to show what the particles are doing.

title: Build an Atom
desc: The child builds an atom by adding protons, neutrons and electrons and watches which element it becomes and how its charge and mass change, then plays a short game to test themselves.
how: For an older child who has asked what everything is made of; play the game together.

title: Reactants, Products and Leftovers
desc: The child makes sandwiches from ingredients to see how many can be made and what is left over, then does the same with molecules in simple chemical reactions, and plays a game.
how: Start with the sandwich screen; it explains reactions with something every child knows.

title: Sugar and Salt Solutions
desc: The child adds sugar or salt to water, evaporates the water away, and zooms in to see how each one dissolves.
how: Pair it with stirring salt and sugar into real glasses of water and leaving one in the sun to evaporate.

title: Gases Intro
desc: The child pumps gas particles into a box, then makes the box bigger or smaller and adds or removes heat to see how the particles and the pressure change.
how: Use when talking about why a football or cycle tyre feels harder after pumping.

title: Density
desc: The child changes the mass and size of blocks, drops them in water to see which float and which sink, and plays detective to work out what a mystery block is made of.
how: Follow up with a tub of water and things from around the house to sort into floaters and sinkers.

title: Exploring Floating and Sinking activity sheet
desc: A printable sheet to use with the PhET Density sim: the child predicts whether blocks will sink or float, works out density from mass and volume, and predicts what happens when a block's size changes.
how: Print it and keep it next to the screen while the child uses the Density sim.

title: Buoyancy: Basics
desc: The child changes a block's size and mass, puts it into different liquids, and sees the forces pushing on it and whether it floats or sinks.
how: Good for the 'upthrust' topic; ask the child to predict before each drop.

title: Forces and Motion: Basics
desc: The child plays tug-of-war with teams of pullers, pushes a crate, fridge or person, and turns friction up or down to see how pushes and pulls change how things move.
how: Start with the tug-of-war screen; it works even for younger children learning push and pull.

title: Balancing Act
desc: The child places bricks and people of different weights on a see-saw to make the plank balance, then tries the Balance Challenge game.
how: Try it after a trip to the park see-saw; ask where a lighter child should sit to balance a heavier one.

title: Gravity Force Lab: Basics
desc: The child changes the mass of two objects and the distance between them and sees how strongly gravity pulls them together.
how: Use when the child asks why things fall or why the Moon stays near Earth.

title: Gravity and Orbits
desc: The child moves the Sun, Earth, Moon and a space station to see how gravity shapes their paths, compares their sizes and distances, and turns gravity off to see what happens.
how: Turning gravity off is the memorable moment; ask the child to guess first.

title: My Solar System
desc: The child sets the starting positions, speeds and masses of two, three or four bodies and watches them orbit each other.
how: For an older child who has enjoyed Gravity and Orbits and wants to build their own system.

title: Magnets and Electromagnets
desc: The child moves a compass around a bar magnet to see the magnetic field, then builds an electromagnet from a battery and a coil of wire.
how: Use after playing with real fridge magnets and a compass.

title: Energy Skate Park: Basics
desc: The child builds ramps and tracks for a skateboarder and watches bar and pie charts show energy changing as the skater rolls up and down.
how: Let the child build tracks freely first, then switch on the energy charts.

title: Energy Forms and Changes
desc: The child heats and cools iron, brick, water and olive oil to see energy move between objects, and links up energy sources, changers and users, such as the Sun, a solar panel and a light bulb.
how: Use the systems screen when studying sources of energy.

title: Greenhouse Effect
desc: The child changes the amount of greenhouse gases in the air, adds clouds, and watches the Earth's temperature go up or down.
how: A starting point for talking about climate change and why caring for the planet matters.

title: Sound Waves
desc: The child sees sound waves spread out from a speaker, changes how high or loud the sound is, and moves a listener around to hear what they would hear.
how: Turn the sound on and let the child connect what they hear with what they see.

title: Waves Intro
desc: The child makes waves with a dripping tap, a speaker or a laser, changes how fast and how big they are, hears the speaker's tone, and finds out what decides the colour of light.
how: Start with the water screen, then compare it with the sound screen.

title: Color Vision
desc: The child shines red, green and blue lamps into a person's eyes and mixes them to make every colour of the rainbow, and changes the colour of a single beam of light.
how: Use when learning how we see things; ask which colours make yellow.

title: Bending Light
desc: The child shines a laser from air into water or glass to see the beam bend, and plays with prisms of different shapes to make rainbows.
how: Pair with a pencil in a glass of water, which looks bent for the same reason.

title: Geometric Optics: Basics
desc: The child watches light rays bend through a lens or bounce off a mirror, and moves the object, the lens and the screen to see how the picture changes.
how: Use with a magnifying glass, if you have one, to make a real image on paper.

title: Natural Selection
desc: The child starts with a pair of rabbits, adds changes such as brown fur or long ears, and sees which rabbits survive wolves, tough food or snow over many generations.
how: Ask the child to predict which rabbits will survive in the snow before they start.

title: Natural Selection activity sheet
desc: A printable sheet for the PhET Natural Selection sim that asks the child to produce brown baby rabbits, change ear length and help rabbits adapt to a snowy place.
how: Print it to give structure to a session with the Natural Selection sim.
